workouts.name: Easy Run
workouts.purpose: Aerobic development, recovery between harder sessions and sustainable weekly volume.
workouts.intensity: RPE 2–4. Conversational effort. Pace is normally a range or ceiling, not a target to chase.
workouts.typicalVolume: 30–90 minutes depending on experience and training phase.
workouts.avoidOrModifyWhen: Illness, worsening pain, or unusual fatigue makes even conversational running feel strained.
workouts.progression: Add duration gradually before adding pace. Strides may be added when freshness is good.
workouts.commonMistakes: Running moderate instead of easy; forcing pace in heat or fatigue.

workouts.name: Recovery Run
workouts.purpose: Gentle movement after demanding training without adding meaningful intensity.
workouts.intensity: RPE 1–3. Slower than normal easy pace when required.
workouts.progression: Do not progress for its own sake; the session exists to support recovery.

workouts.name: Easy Run with Strides
workouts.purpose: Aerobic volume plus relaxed neuromuscular speed.
workouts.intensity: Easy running with 4–8 × 15–25 second controlled strides; full easy recovery.
workouts.compatibleWith: Upper-body strength; a following easy day.
workouts.avoidOrModifyWhen: Calf, hamstring or Achilles symptoms are present.
workouts.progression: Add stride repetitions before lengthening them; keep mechanics relaxed.

workouts.name: Continuous Tempo
workouts.purpose: Improve lactate-threshold endurance and sustained pace control.
workouts.intensity: RPE 7–8; comfortably hard. Use current threshold capability, not unsupported goal pace.
workouts.typicalVolume: 15–40 minutes continuous, surrounded by warm-up and cool-down.
workouts.recoveryDemand: Moderate to high; usually 24–48 hours before another demanding run.
workouts.compatibleWith: Upper-body strength later the same day when well tolerated.
workouts.avoidOrModifyWhen: Recovery is poor, heat is extreme, or the required pace cannot be held without racing the session.
workouts.progression: Increase controlled duration before increasing speed.
workouts.commonMistakes: Starting too fast; turning the final section into a time trial.

workouts.name: Cruise Intervals
workouts.purpose: Accumulate threshold work with short recoveries and better pace control than a continuous tempo.
workouts.intensity: RPE 7–8. Examples include 3 × 10 minutes, 4 × 2 km or 5–6 × 1 mile with short jogging recovery.
workouts.progression: Add total threshold time or reduce recovery slightly before increasing pace.

workouts.name: VO2-Max Intervals
workouts.purpose: Develop high-end aerobic power and running economy.
workouts.intensity: RPE 8–9. Repetitions commonly last 2–5 minutes with controlled jogging recovery.
workouts.recoveryDemand: High; avoid placing near another hard run, heavy lower-body lifting or intense soccer.
workouts.progression: Increase repeat count before making repeats faster. Stop when pace or mechanics deteriorate materially.

workouts.name: Hill Repeats
workouts.purpose: Running-specific strength, mechanics and aerobic power with less absolute speed.
workouts.intensity: Depends on format: short powerful hills or longer controlled aerobic repetitions.
workouts.recoveryDemand: Moderate to high, especially for calves and posterior chain.
workouts.avoidOrModifyWhen: Achilles, calf or hamstring symptoms are active.

workouts.name: Fartlek
workouts.purpose: Flexible speed development with effort-based changes rather than rigid splits.
workouts.intensity: Variable; hard portions normally RPE 6–9 depending on the workout purpose.

workouts.name: Easy Long Run
workouts.purpose: Aerobic endurance, musculoskeletal durability and fuelling practice.
workouts.typicalVolume: Goal- and experience-dependent. Increase conservatively and account for total weekly load.
workouts.recoveryDemand: Moderate to high based on duration.
workouts.avoidOrModifyWhen: Heavy lower-body strength within the preceding 24–48 hours when long-run quality matters.
workouts.progression: Increase duration gradually, then introduce controlled quality only after the distance is well tolerated.

workouts.name: Progressive Long Run
workouts.purpose: Endurance plus controlled late-run pace development.
workouts.intensity: Begin easy; finish steady or moderately hard without racing.
workouts.progression: Extend the steady finish gradually while preserving an easy opening section.

workouts.name: Marathon-Pace Long Run
workouts.purpose: Marathon-specific endurance, pacing, fuelling and confidence.
workouts.intensity: Easy running plus one or more blocks at a realistic current marathon-effort range.
workouts.avoidOrModifyWhen: Goal pace is unsupported by current fitness, recovery is poor, or environmental conditions make pace misleading.
workouts.progression: Increase total marathon-pace volume gradually before using longer continuous blocks.

workouts.name: Tune-Up / Sharpening Session
workouts.purpose: Maintain speed and rhythm while reducing overall training load near a race.
workouts.intensity: Brief controlled quality; never a maximal test.

workouts.name: Upper Push
workouts.purpose: Maintain or develop chest, shoulder and triceps strength with minimal direct lower-body fatigue.
workouts.intensity: Mostly 1–3 reps in reserve; avoid unnecessary failure when a key run follows within 24 hours.
workouts.recoveryDemand: Moderate upper-body fatigue; low running interference.
workouts.compatibleWith: Easy runs, recovery runs and many quality-run days when scheduled after running.

workouts.name: Upper Pull
workouts.purpose: Back, rear-deltoid and biceps strength and muscle balance.
workouts.recoveryDemand: Moderate upper-body fatigue; generally low running interference.
workouts.compatibleWith: Easy running and quality-run days when grip or back fatigue does not affect running posture.

workouts.name: Arms
workouts.purpose: Direct biceps and triceps development with negligible leg fatigue.
workouts.intensity: 1–2 reps in reserve on most sets; final isolation sets may approach failure when recovery is good.
workouts.compatibleWith: Easy runs and the day before a long run, provided the session does not become excessively long or exhausting.

workouts.name: Lower Strength
workouts.purpose: Maintain or build force production and tissue capacity for hips, knees, hamstrings and calves.
workouts.intensity: Usually 1–3 reps in reserve. Marathon-focused phases should favour quality and consistency over maximal fatigue.
workouts.typicalVolume: 8–16 working sets depending on the training phase.
workouts.recoveryDemand: High; commonly 24–72 hours depending on load, exercise selection and training age.
workouts.compatibleWith: Easy or recovery running when well tolerated.
workouts.avoidOrModifyWhen: Important intervals, marathon-pace long runs or races within the next 24–48 hours.
workouts.progression: Add load or repetitions conservatively while monitoring soreness, gait and key-run quality.

workouts.name: Marathon Maintenance Strength
workouts.purpose: Preserve strength and tissue capacity during high running volume with reduced soreness and interference.
workouts.intensity: Moderate to heavy but low volume; avoid grinding repetitions.
workouts.progression: Maintain load where possible; reduce sets before reducing useful intensity during peak running weeks.

workouts.name: Core and Trunk
workouts.purpose: Trunk stiffness, load transfer and tolerance without large systemic fatigue.

workouts.name: Indoor Futsal
workouts.purpose: Team sport, enjoyment, agility and repeated high-intensity running.
workouts.loadProfile: Treat as a quality running session rather than easy cross-training. Repeated acceleration, deceleration and change of direction can create substantial calf, hamstring, knee and adductor load.
workouts.planningGuidance: Avoid stacking with hard intervals or heavy lower-body strength immediately before or after when possible. A long run followed by futsal may be tolerated by an experienced athlete but should be treated as a demanding combined day.

workouts.name: Outdoor Soccer Match
workouts.purpose: Competitive match play that develops soccer-specific fitness through repeated high-intensity efforts, sprinting, change of direction and sustained aerobic work.
workouts.loadProfile: High variability with sprinting, collisions and large total movement volume.
workouts.planningGuidance: Usually replace, rather than add to, another hard running session that week. Avoid placing immediately before a key long run, race or heavy lower-body strength session where possible.

workouts.name: Easy Cycling
workouts.purpose: Low-impact aerobic work or active recovery.
workouts.recoveryDemand: Low, unless duration or hills are substantial.

workouts.name: Recovery Walk
workouts.purpose: Gentle movement, circulation and mental recovery.

workouts.name: Mobility Session
workouts.purpose: Maintain comfortable range of motion and address stiffness without forcing end range.
